note.question: How do multiple parts facing stochastic demands and adopt procure/manufacture-to-stock and print-on-demand to highlight the main difference of production modes featured in traditional manufacturing and 3-D printing compare?
note.overview: We present a general framework to study the design of spare parts logistics in the presence of three-dimensional (3-D) printing technology. The model considers multiple parts facing stochastic demands and adopt procure/manufacture-to-stock versus print-on-demand to highlight the main difference of production modes featured in traditional manufacturing and 3-D printing. To minimize long-run average system cost, our model determines which parts to stock and which to print.
